column2: not men. Men must have a low regard for a prophet of the Lord when they think they can influence the message he is to deliver."

column2: “Behold

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Crônicas;18;26;26. Return in Peace;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;26. Return in peace. Ahab was endeavoring to put on a brave front. Antigo Testamento;2 Crônicas;18;27;27. If Thou Certainly Return;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;27. If thou certainly return. The prophecy would be tested by its fulfillment (see Deut. 18:22). The death of Ahab (2 Chron. 18:34) was the vindication of the prophet Micaiah.

Antigo Testamento;2 Crônicas;18;28;28. So the King;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"27. If thou certainly return. The prophecy would be tested by its fulfillment (see Deut. 18:22). The death of Ahab (2 Chron. 18:34) was the vindication of the prophet Micaiah.
28. So the king. Jehoshaphat found himself in strange company and in strange circumstances. He had asked for a prophet of the Lord

Antigo Testamento;2 Crônicas;19;1;1. And Jehoshaphat;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"1. And Jehoshaphat. Chapter 19 contains materials not appearing in the record of Kings. It includes such items as the prophetic rebuke of Jehoshaphat after his return from Ramoth-gilead (vs. 1–3)

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Crônicas;19;2;2. Jehu the Son of Hanani;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"2. Jehu the son of Hanani. Hanani was the name of the prophet who had rebuked Asa for relying on the king of Syria rather than on the Lord

column3: Ammon
column4: and Mt. Seir and the wrecking of Jehoshaphat’s navy."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Crônicas;19;6;6. Take Heed;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"6. Take heed. Jehoshaphat urged the new judges to consider the importance of their work. They were to administer justice impartially to all classes

With you. God is interested in justice and is present in the courtroom. He marks every impartial verdict and notes every breach of justice."

Antigo Testamento;2 Crônicas;19;7;7. Fear of the Lord;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"7. Fear of the Lord. The man who has the responsibility of administering justice constantly faces the task of deciding cases
column2: and he must do his work in recognition of the fact that the eyes of the Lord are upon him. He must constantly settle matters in dispute
column3: and in so doing he must remember that every decision he makes is registered in the books of heaven.

column1: No iniquity. It is a comfort to remember that the great Judge of the world is a righteous judge and therefore His every decision is true and righteous (see Deut. 32:4; Ps. 9:8; 67:4; 96:13; Rev. 19:11).

Nor respect of persons. A righteous judge decides every case on its merits rather than according to the personalities involved. Altogether too often there is “respect of persons” in the matter of rendering decisions. Personal friends are favored
column2: and those in a position to return favors are shown special considerations. Such judgments are neither impartial nor righteous
column3: nor do they bring the blessing of Heaven. The Lord of heaven is no respecter of persons (Deut. 10:17; Acts 10:34; Rom. 2:11; Gal. 2:6; Eph. 6:9; 1 Peter 1:17)
column4: and His followers are to be like Him. The practice of flattering and favoring men of wealth and position while despising and defrauding those who are poor and humble

Many an individual in a position of trust has been bought off by accepting some seemingly innocent token. Every man faced with the responsibility of making decisions must ever be on the alert that he does not allow a gift of any nature to be the determining factor in the verdict rendered."

column1: A word of caution should be added. According to one commentator the Song of Solomon has been the “happy hunting ground” of allegorists for many centuries. The introduction of the allegorization of Scriptures into the Christian church can be traced back to the Alexandrian school in Egypt and particularly to Origen (c. A.D. 184–c. 254) as the first great exponent of this method. The system grew out of a fusion between Greek philosophy and Christianity. The method has persisted with varying degrees of virility ever since. As an illustration of the extreme lengths to which such methods tend are the following examples drawn from various allegorical interpreters of the Song of Solomon: the kiss of Christ—the incarnation; the cheeks of the bride—outward Christianity and good works; her golden chains—faith; spikenard—redeemed humanity; the hair of the bride like a flock of goats—the nations converted to Christianity; the 80 wives of Solomon—the admission of the Gentile nations to Christianity; the navel of the Shulamite—the cup from which the church refreshes those that thirst for salvation; the two breasts—the Old and New Testaments.

The folly of such a method is that it assumes a license for figurative interpretations without providing criteria to control it. It offers as the validity of an interpretation only the imagination of its exponent. True
column2: there may be a general attempt to make conclusions conform to the analogy of Scripture
column3: but the attempt is too weak to hold the interpreter’s imagination in check.

ELLEN G. WHITE COMMENTS
PSALM 106
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 106 is generally considered a sequel to Ps. 105. It is a national hymn of Israel
column2: and like Ps. 105 reviews Israel’s early history to show God’s faithfulness to the covenant. However
column3: it has this striking difference: the psalmist shows how chronic was Israel’s disloyalty and what awful consequences she suffered as a result of her sins. The psalm covers the history of Israel from Egypt through the wilderness wandering
column4: and her history in the Holy Land through the period of the judges. This hymn exhibits a swing of thought between the weakness and folly of Israel and the strength of God as shown both in deliverance and in punishment
column5: in alternating unequal stanzas. It begins and closes with praise and prayer. The psalm is the first of the so-called hallelujah psalms (see also Ps. 111–113; 117; 135; 146–150). Like Ps. 105
column6: Ps. 106 should be studied in the light of 8T 107–116; TM 98; and LS 196."

Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;101;101. Refrained;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"100. The ancients. Those who apply themselves diligently to a study of God’s Word have more real knowledge than the aged philosopher who has not stooped to drink at the source of all true wisdom (see on v. 98).
101. Refrained. David endeavored to avoid that which would hinder his spiritual progress. The bypaths of sin may be smooth and flowery
column2: but those who are allured by them forsake the Word of God."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;103;103. Sweet;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"103. Sweet. Not only had the psalmist listened to the words of God; he had fed upon them. They were sweeter than honey to him (see Ps. 19:10)."
Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;104;104. Understanding;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"104. Understanding. The man of true understanding detests sin and falsehood
column2: and loves righteousness and truth."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;105;105. Lamp;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;105. Lamp. The Word of God illuminates the way so that men may walk safely in the spiritual darkness of this world. He who has this light to guide him need not stumble even though his path is beset with evil (see 2 Peter 1:19).
Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;106;106. I Will Perform;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"106. I will perform. The psalmist pledged to obey the law
column2: and manifested great care in carrying out this pledge. Similarly we should put forth every effort to cooperate with God and to keep every worth-while resolution of the heart."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;107;107. Afflicted;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;107. Afflicted. Service to God does not guarantee freedom from difficulties or sufferings (Phil. 1:29). Trials develop noble characters.

Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;108;108. Of My Mouth;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;108. Of my mouth. Evidently offerings of thanksgiving and prayer. The writer pleads with the Lord to accept these as he offers them willingly. The Lord delights in voluntary offerings.

Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;109;109. In My Hand;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"108. Of my mouth. Evidently offerings of thanksgiving and prayer. The writer pleads with the Lord to accept these as he offers them willingly. The Lord delights in voluntary offerings.
109. In my hand. A figure of peril (see 1 Sam. 19:5). The psalmist expresses his resolve not to turn aside to find safety in sin and thus forget the law; he will risk his life
column2: if need be
column3: for the sake of the law."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;112;112. Inclined Mine Heart;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;112. Inclined mine heart. See on Ps. 66:18.

Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;114;114. Hiding Place;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"114. Hiding place. When we are beset with temptation we can find our refuge in God. When the darts of the enemy are being hurled at us

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;115;115. Depart From Me;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"115. Depart from me. See 1 Cor. 5:9; 2 Thess. 3:14. David is anxious not to be in the company of the wicked
column2: for they stunt his spiritual growth. It is well to cultivate the friendship of those whose influence elevates to a higher level of spirituality."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;116;116. That I May Live;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;116. That I may live. The psalmist felt that he was so dependent upon God’s sustaining power that he could not live without it.
Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;0;Not Be Ashamed;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"Not be ashamed. We need never be ashamed of our hope
column2: for it rests upon the sure foundation of God’s Word (see Rom. 5:5; Phil. 1:20; 1 John 2:28)."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;117;117. Continually;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;117. Continually. The ability to persevere to the end comes through divine power (see Jude 24).
Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;118;118. Trodden Down;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"118. Trodden down. Or
column2: “rejected
column3: ” “tossed aside.” By their own choice the wicked destroy themselves (see 5T 120; cf. Hosea 13:9). They have no desire to walk with God
column4: and God has no alternative other than to destroy them."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;119;119. Like Dross;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"119. Like dross. The dross and the precious metal are together now
column2: but soon there will come a day of separation
column3: when the Refiner will accomplish His work of purification (Mal. 3:3; cf. Matt. 13:30)."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;120;120. AM Afraid;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"120. Am afraid. See on Ps. 19:9; Prov. 1:7."

Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;121;121. Judgment and Justice;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"121. Judgment and justice. In the matter of which David was accused his conscience was clear. He had endeavored to be just in his dealings with his fellow men. He had done the best he could

column2: and confidently expected that the Lord would answer his prayer. He appealed to the great Judge to be delivered from the injustice of his oppressors.

column1: 122. Be surety. Compare Gen. 43:9."

Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;123;123. Word of Thy Righteousness;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"123. Word of thy righteousness. The psalmist longed to hear the righteous judgment of God concerning him. His enemies had maligned his character and tried to bring disrepute upon him
column2: but he knew that God would speak justly concerning him."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;125;125. Thy Servant;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"125. Thy servant. The psalmist delighted to call himself the “servant” of God (see Ps. 19:11

column2: God is long-suffering and slow to destroy anyone. He longs for all to repent and turn from their evil way (see Eze. 33:11; 2 Peter 3:9)."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;127;127. Above Fine Gold;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;127. Above fine gold. The best of earthly possessions are not to be compared with the treasures of God’s Word.

Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;128;128. Every False Way;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"128. Every false way. A love for truth is accompanied by a hatred for falsehood. Truth and falsehood are mutually exclusive. The very fact that we love the truth causes us to hate error. “When we are clothed with the righteousness of Christ
column2: we shall have no relish for sin” (EGW RH March 18

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;129;129. Wonderful;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"129. Wonderful. pela’oth

column3: 14). The words of God and the acts of God are closely allied."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;130;130. Simple;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"130. Simple. See on Ps. 19:7. Those in need of instruction
column2: who sense their lack
column3: are given discernment by a study of the Word (see on Prov. 1:4)."

column2: “according to judgment
column3: ” possibly in the sense of “according to the right of.” Those who love the name of God have a right to call upon Him. The Lord is pleased when we bring our petitions to Him and claim His promises."

column2: “according to judgment

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;138;138. Hast Commanded;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"138. Hast commanded. A divine authority has formed the testimonies
column2: and they bear the impress of their Maker. It is not for man to question these royal commands. They are righteous and faithful

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;139;139. My Zeal Hath Consumed Me;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;139. My zeal hath consumed me. See on Ps. 69:9.
Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;140;140. Very Pure;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"140. Very pure. Literally
column2: “exceedingly refined.” In the Word of God there is no mixture of error."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;141;141. Small and Despised;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;141. Small and despised. David was willing to place a low estimate upon himself. Great men are never great in their own estimation.

column2: but the truth itself; not only does it contain the truth

column2: but sprang from an inward peace
column3: a peace derived from a study of the Word of God."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;144;144. Everlasting;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"144. Everlasting. Men change their laws to conform to changing standards
column2: but the law of God is unchangeable."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;0;Give Me Understanding;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;Give me understanding. Man can truly understand the purpose of his being only when he lives in harmony with the law of God (see John 7:17).

column2: whereas lip service is unavailing."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;147;147. I Prevented the Dawning;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"147. I prevented the dawning. That is

column2: “precede” (see on v. 147). The night was commonly divided into three watches (Lam. 2:19; see on Judges 7:19; 1 Sam. 11:11). The psalmist likens himself to one listed for duty during these night watches. Before the time of his appointment he is awake and meditating upon God’s Word."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;149;149. According to;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;149. According to. We should ask God to answer our prayers not according to our desires but in the light of His all-wise providence.

column2: but to help."

David was passing through severe trial and appealed his case to God for help. No child of God in affliction ever cries to the Lord in vain. God may not grant the desired deliverance
column2: but He will provide courage and faith to endure the test (see 2 Cor. 12:7–9)."

Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;155;155. Far From the Wicked;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"155. Far from the wicked. Every step the sinner takes along the path of evil removes him farther from God’s saving grace. Unless he alters his course
column2: he finally reaches the place where mercy no longer lingers (see 5T 119

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;156;156. Tender Mercies;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"156. Tender mercies. Or
column2: “compassions.”"

column2: “to feel a loathing.” As the psalmist watched the ways of the wicked he was repelled by their conduct."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;160;160. From the Beginning;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"160. From the beginning. Heb. ro’sh
column2: literally
column3: “head
column4: ” here probably in the sense of “sum” as ro’sh is translated in Ps. 139:17."

The persons who should have sympathized with David were among his most bitter opponents. These royal leaders were appointed to avenge the oppressed and to protect the helpless. Instead of performing their duty
column2: they spent their time persecuting the righteous."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;162;162. Great Spoil;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;162. Great spoil. Compare Isa. 9:3.

column2: in sorrow
column3: or in joy his voice was uplifted in thankful hymns of praise."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;165;165. Great Peace;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"165. Great peace. Though there is turmoil and strife without
column2: there is peace in the heart of him who loves the law of God."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;0;Nothing Shall Offend Them;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"Nothing shall offend them. Literally
column2: “nothing is to them a stumbling block.” Those who love the law have no occasion of stumbling. They walk with firm and steady step along the straight path of God’s law and do not turn aside to the bypaths of sin."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;166;166. I Have Hoped;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"166. I have hoped. David fixed his hope upon God. He looked to Him alone for salvation
column2: and put forth earnest effort to obey the commandments."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;168;168. Before Thee;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"168. Before thee. There is nothing hidden from God’s sight (Heb. 4:13). How comforting the thought that when we are misunderstood by men
column2: our ways are known to God!"

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;170;170. Supplication;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"170. Supplication. Heb. techinnah
column2: “a supplication for favor.”"

column2: “to bubble
column3: ” or “pour forth.” The psalmist desires that from his life and his lips will ever proceed songs of grateful praise."

column1: Antigo Testamento;Salmos;119;172;172. Righteousness;Comentário Bíblico Adventista III;"172. Righteousness. Not only are the commandments right in themselves
column2: they are the essence of righteousness. “The law is holy

column4: and just [literally

column2: like David
column3: choose the precepts of God as their guide."

PSALM 129INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 129 is a song celebrating national deliverance. The psalmist speaks of the trials through which Israel as a nation had passed and of how the Lord interposed on their behalf and brought confusion to their enemies. It is a song of the countryside and has many allusions to agricultural pursuits. The precise historical incident that may have been the occasion of this psalm is a matter of conjecture. The psalmist is not so much concerned with the incident as with the lesson to be drawn from it.
